nonblockingWork.description: Unresolved work that does not block F1 gate status. Each item is recorded here and mapped to the future task that will resolve it. None of these items represent silent omissions — each is documented at its source location.

items.title: Legacy write path not cut over to AuthorityCommandBus — F2 blocker
items.description: The legacy WritePolicy → stores write path (KriaMemoryRuntime fact/snippet/document-chunk writes, GoalStore direct writes, the legacy Memory write-policy path) was NOT cut over to the AuthorityCommandBus in F1 because the F2 semantic builders (typed AuthorityTx commands for Memory/Entity/Goal/Relationship records) do not yet exist. Routing the live path to an empty command bus would silently drop the user's existing memory. The governed write boundary (AuthorityCommandBus, AuthorityTx) is fully implemented and proven correct; it awaits F2 record types to become the live path.
items.evidenceLocation: crates/kria-core/src/memory/model/legacy_mapping.rs — Removal ledger: every legacy struct has a live consumer, gate F1.5 write + F3 read; crates/kria-core/src/memory/authority/bus.rs AuthorityCommandBus::submit_deferred
items.blockedBy: F2 semantic model (tasks 2.1.x — typed cognitive records and provenance)

items.title: Free-text relationship table not replaced with registry-governed relationships — F2.2 blocker
items.description: The legacy types::Relationship free-text edge and ad-hoc GraphStore read model have not been replaced. The Relation_Registry schema (migration 0018/0019/0020), registry seed rows, and the canonical relationship identity hash are implemented, but the full governed create/edit/expire/delete/restore/undo commands (task 2.2.5) and legacy migration/reconciliation (2.2.6) and deletion of legacy tables (2.2.7) are not yet done. The registry-governed path exists and is tested; the live graph read still uses the legacy types::Relationship table.
items.blockedBy: F2.2 canonical relation registry and Memory Links (tasks 2.2.5–2.2.7)

items.title: Retrieval-on-v2 not implemented; contract-layer reads unfiltered by caller policy partition — F3 blocker
items.description: The read_authorization gate (policy::read_authorization::authorize_read / AuthorizedScope / ScopePredicate) was implemented and is unit-tested, but is called from nowhere in contract.rs, retriever.rs, api.rs, or graph_intel.rs. Every contract::* read function and the MemorySystem methods they delegate to take no CallerContext/PolicyPartition parameter and query the whole authority DB. Today this is safe only because of the single-partition-caller assumption (single-user, single-laptop deployment; LocalDesktop and AuthenticatedRemote share one static [server].caller partition). It stops being safe once two distinct-partition callers are admitted to the same server — see the F1.6.5 audit note in memory_routes.rs. Additionally, all live reads still use the legacy v1 tables (facts/snippets/conversation), not the v2 records/entities_v2/goals_v2 tables, because retrieval-on-v2 is an F3 deliverable.
items.evidenceLocation: crates/kria-server/src/memory_routes.rs — F1.6.5 audit note at module top (lines 9–101); crates/kria-core/src/memory/policy/read_authorization.rs
items.blockedBy: F3 retrieval, cognition, and canonical API (tasks 3.x)

items.title: Token issuance gap — no HTTP endpoint or pairing flow to issue tokens to real remote clients
items.description: auth.rs::issue_token() mints HMAC-SHA256 bearer tokens and is exercised by unit tests, but there is no HTTP endpoint, operator CLI, or device-pairing flow wired up to hand a token to a legitimate remote client. Remote access requires the [server].jwt_secret to be set and remote-enabled=true (both checked before bind_security accepts connections), but the mechanism for a real operator or device to obtain a token through a normal flow does not yet exist. The module-level doc comment in auth.rs explicitly records this as a documented gap, not a silent omission. This is mapped to future 1.6.x work.
items.evidenceLocation: crates/kria-server/src/auth.rs — module-level doc comment lines 28–36: 'there is no HTTP endpoint or operator tooling wired up yet to hand a token to a legitimate remote client — that is a documented gap, not silently missing.'

items.title: Crypto shredding capability is unavailable
items.description: CRYPTO_SHRED_CAPABILITY = "unavailable — payload encryption not yet implemented; reliance on host OS disk encryption only". This is the correct honest state: the shred_keys table and ShredKey model exist (migration 0014), lifecycle::shred_subject() models key ID/version/status/destruction-proof without storing secret bytes, and all UI/API/health paths report the 'unavailable' wording. No false Crypto-Shredded claim exists anywhere. Actual cryptographic shredding requires payload-level encryption, external key storage, and provable destruction — none of which is implemented. This will remain unavailable unless encryption is explicitly prioritized in a future task.
items.evidenceLocation: crates/kria-core/src/memory/api.rs:45 — pub const CRYPTO_SHRED_CAPABILITY; crates/kria-core/src/memory/lifecycle.rs — shred_subject doc comment lines 1628–1672
items.blockedBy: Future payload encryption implementation (if ever prioritized)
